title: Built a parametric circular-grating SVG icon generator (context/figures/grating.py), verified in a real browser; not yet wired into any figure

claims.text: context/figures/grating.py generates a circular-aperture grating icon as native SVG (clipPath circle + rotated square-wave stripe rects), parametric on radius, n_cycles, orientation, colors, duty cycle. Also includes omission_marker() (dashed-circle placeholder matching the paradigm figure's existing omission convention). build_demo() renders a 10-icon sample sheet (orientation sweep 0/45/90/135deg, spatial-frequency sweep 2/4/6/8 cycles, real vs omitted). Verified correct in a real browser (Claude_Browser preview) -- clean circular apertures, correctly rotated stripes, correctly clipped.
claims.receipt: python grating.py: 'wrote grating_demo.svg 420x340'; browser screenshot confirmed all 10 icons render correctly (clean circles, correct stripe rotation per orientation, correct cycle count per frequency setting, dashed-circle omission marker)

claims.text: The svglib->PDF->pymupdf rendering pipeline used elsewhere this session (fig01's verification) FAILS SILENTLY on <clipPath> containing a <circle> -- confirmed by rendering the same grating_demo.svg through both svglib (completely unclipped, all 10 icons' stripe rects overlapping across the whole canvas) and a real browser (correct). Earlier in the session, svglib was already known to mis-handle MULTI-shape (2-rect) clipPaths; this extends the known limitation to single-shape NON-RECT clipPaths too. Single-rect clipPaths (used throughout fig01's script) remain confirmed safe.
claims.receipt: side-by-side comparison: svglib render of grating_demo.svg showed all stripes unclipped and overlapping (screenshot taken); Claude_Browser render of the identical file showed all 10 icons correctly clipped to their circles

issues: Not yet integrated into any figure. fig01/fig02's existing stimulus icons are still the raster diamond/square stripe shapes baked into the Illustrator sources -- replacing them with this vector generator (if wanted) requires editing those figures' scripts, not done in this pass.

svglib is now confirmed unreliable for verifying ANY figure that uses a non-rect or multi-shape clipPath. Future verification of such figures should use the Claude_Browser preview pane, not the svglib/pymupdf fallback pipeline, or should avoid non-rect clips in the first place.
